note:
AUA/ASCO/ASTRO/SUO: treatment of non-metastatic muscle-invasive bladder cancer, 2017 amended 2020 and 2024. The whole document is one disease setting -- its title says non-metastatic MIBC and it never leaves it -- so the setting is carried by the default and the rules below are almost entirely exclusions.

**The document says everything twice.** AUA's format is a summary of the guideline statements followed by the full discussion, under identical headings: `GUIDELINE STATEMENTS > INITIAL PATIENT EVALUATION AND COUNSELING` appears once with one passage and again with six. Both are real content -- the first is the statement, the second is the evidence for it -- so nothing here pins an occurrence. What that does mean is that any exclusion has to claim `every_occurrence`, or it removes the front matter from the summary and leaves the identical block in the discussion.

default.note: The document's own title. Metastatic disease is out of its scope and is covered by the EAU metastatic guideline already in the corpus.

rules.note: 18 passages, the single largest block in the document.
Claims the whole closing chapter: panel rosters, conflict-of-interest disclosures, peer reviewers and the disclaimer. Not leaf-matched, because it is the chapter and its twelve subsections that go.
Catches the 2020 and 2024 rosters in the front matter with one rule. The identically named subsections inside the closing chapter are already claimed above; this reaches the front-matter copies.

rules.match_section: Assessment of the Risk of Bias of Individual Studies
rules.note: How AUA graded its evidence, including the nomenclature linking statement type to evidence strength. It describes the method that produced the recommendations rather than any recommendation, and a panel asking what to do for a patient should never retrieve it.
Substring, so it claims both the front-matter `Methodology` and the `METHODOLOGY` chapter with its systematic-review and data-extraction subsections.
